title: SAML2 federation bootstrap: metadata exchange validation, RBAC-v2 mapping, and audit hooks
creator: Lucia Morales
description:
Implement a SAML 2.0 federation bootstrap flow that securely exchanges and validates IdP/SP metadata, generates an RBAC-v2 role mapping template, and emits tamper-evident audit events for admin review. The feature is intended for Dedicated and Private customers who require fast, low-friction SSO setup but need strong provenance, admin guardrails, and auditable onboarding.

Scope:
- Add a 'Federation Bootstrap' flow in the console to accept metadata (file upload or URL) and perform multi-stage validation: signature verification, certificate chain checks, entityID canonicalization, and schema conformance.
- Produce a signed metadata digest and provenance record (who uploaded, where from, timestamp, validation steps) that is stored in the audit log.
- Provide RBAC-v2 mapping suggestions derived from metadata attributes (attribute names -> Redwood role templates) with confidence scores and a preview of effective permissions. Admins can accept, modify, or create mappings.
- Add an assertion replay simulator (dry-run) that lets operators run sample SAML responses through the mapping to validate the end-to-end transformation without enabling it in production.
- Emit structured audit events for: metadata ingestion, validation failures, mapping changes, dry-run results, and final enable/disable actions. Audit payloads must include metadata digest and validation trace id.

Non-goals: automated trust-by-default or silent mapping changes; full IdP discovery protocols (this is metadata-first).

Trade-offs & decisions:
- Synchronous full validation on upload increases latency for large metadata bundles; decided to run heavy crypto checks in a background worker and return a short-lived verification token for the console to poll. Critical certificate errors fail fast.
- We will store only signed digests and provenance in the main control plane; full original metadata bundle can be optionally archived to customer-controlled storage for privacy/compliance.
- RBAC mapping will be suggestions only (no auto-apply) to respect least-privilege.

Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SO/SAML2+Federation+Bootstrap (draft)
- Proto UI mock: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/sso-bootstrap-proto
- Spike PR (validation worker): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4123
acceptance_criteria: Console flow accepts metadata (URL or file) and returns a verification token
Background worker performs signature and cert-chain validation; results visible in console timeline
RBAC-v2 mapping suggestions are generated and editable; admin can preview dry-run results
Audit log contains structured events for ingestion, validation steps, mapping changes, and enable actions
Dry-run assertion simulator produces human-readable mismatch diagnostics and stable trace IDs for post-mortem
